longForm.overview:
💍 is the emoji of marriage coded ring read — a clean ring-pulse shape, the marriage filled-in silhouette, and the universal 'marriage ring' tag for marriage-marker. Where ⬛ reads as solid-black-coded ring read and ⬜ reads as solid-white-coded ring read, 💍 captures the moment when the sender wants to communicate marriage coded ring — a 'marriage 💍' marriage-marker marker or a 'ring-pulse pulse 💍' marriage-marker reveal. The marriage fill cue borrows from design-coded bullet lists and the modern marriage-marker aesthetic, which is exactly why the emoji reads as marriage coded rather than literal ring-coded shape.

In real-world usage 💍 lives in the spaces where the sender wants to communicate marriage-marker energy. A partner sends it on a 'marriage 💍' marriage-marker marker. A friend sends it on a 'ring-pulse pulse 💍' reveal. A coworker sends it on a 'marriage coded 💍' list thread. The marriage fill cue is what makes the emoji feel marriage coded — it is not just 'shape,' it is 'marriage coded ring moment.'

What separates 💍 from the rest of the shape family is the marriage register. The emoji is not saying 'solid-black' (⬛), 'solid-white' (⬜), or 'solid-square' (◼). It is saying 'marriage coded ring,' which carries a specific design-coded tradition. That is why 💍 travels especially well on partner marriage-marker markers, marriage-marker reveals, and any context where the sender wants the message to land with marriage energy.

longForm.whenNotToUse:
Skip 💍 in sympathy, condolence, or break-up contexts. The marriage coded ring cue is the wrong tone for any conversation where the moment is somber. A quiet ❤️ or a sentence that acknowledges the moment is a better fit.

Avoid 💍 in 'literal object' or finish-coded contexts where the marriage energy feels off. A 'marriage 💍' message works for marriage-marker marker; for finish-coded contexts use 🏁 or a sentence.

Skip 💍 when you want to communicate a different color. The marriage coded register is too marriage-coded for moments that need a literal neutral fill; use ⬛ or ⬜ when the design needs to land clean.
longForm.howToReply:
If someone sends 💍, the cleanest mirror is another 💍, ⬛, or a sentence that joins the marriage energy. If you want to escalate the engagement, follow with a sentence that adds context: 'marriage for sure' or 'ring-pulse pulse together.' If the ring cue feels too marriage coded, reply with a sharper emoji (◼ or ◻) that signals shape-coded energy without matching the marriage volume.

When 💍 lands as a partner 'marriage 💍' marriage-marker marker, mirror with another 💍, a heart emoji, or a sentence that escalates the romance. When it arrives as a 'ring-pulse pulse 💍' list thread, mirror with another 💍, a sentence that joins the team energy, or a heart emoji that matches.
